conflicts: Included feet: Juki's manual lists a zipper foot, an even feed foot and a 1/4 in quilting foot as standard and the 1/5 in quilting foot as optional. At least four review pages and dealers say both quilting feet ship with the machine. We follow Juki's list.

Throat: 8.5 in is dealer copy (Sewing Machines Plus, and 8.5 x 6 in on Weidner's TL chart). Juki publishes no needle-to-arm figure, and its machine depth is 8.6 in, so the dealer number may be the depth. Three Reddit comments and one editorial table say about 9 in. We show 8.5 in with this caveat.
Height: Juki's manual gives 35.0 cm (13.8 in); Juki's web page and one dealer listing say 9 in. We use the manual.
Auxiliary table depth: Juki's web page says 13 in (335 mm); its manual says 27.7 cm (10.9 in). We use the manual.
Needle sizes: Juki's web page gives #7 to #18; the manual lists #11 and #14, which reads as the sizes supplied.

Price: Juki's list price is $2,169. Dealers sold new units at $1,239 on 2026-09-30 (Sewing Machines Plus, Weidner). The $900 show model and $1,199 Lowe's figure seen earlier are different or older listings.
Hook type: one dealer spec block says horizontal-axis full-rotary hook; Weidner's TL chart says vertical hook rotary bobbin. The Juki documents we read do not say.

ownerThemes.theme: The automatic needle threader is the most repeated complaint: owners say it is fiddly, stops working or goes unused in favor of threading by hand, while Juki lists it as a feature.
The walking foot that comes with the machine draws more complaints than praise, though some owners report no problems and a few say it improved after a learning period.
Owners describe tension as steady once set, but several needed to adjust it out of the box or when changing between piecing and quilting.
Regular oiling is widely mentioned and mostly accepted as a habit; Juki's manual says daily if used daily, and one owner reports a burning-oil smell after over-oiling.
Speed with a slider for control and power through thick layers are the most consistent praise across Reddit, forums, blogs and dealer reviews.
Owners with years of use report few failures, with defects described as isolated cases such as a faulty foot pedal replaced by the seller.

Buyers who want faster straight stitch and have room for a table price out the true industrial instead.
Quilters who want a 10 in arm but need zigzag and buttonholes compare a computerized flatbed.

editorial.verdict: A straight-stitch-only portable that gives quilters and bag makers industrial-style speed and a thread trimmer without a dedicated table.
editorial.whoFor: Quilters, garment sewists and small-batch makers who already own or do not need a zigzag machine and want a fast, heavy straight stitch.
editorial.skipIf: You need buttonholes, zigzag or stretch stitches from your only machine, or you have no room to store a 25 lb machine plus its auxiliary table.

strengths: Published top speed of 1,500 spm, with a slider that starts at 200 spm for control.

Automatic trimmer on a button and on the pedal heel, and drop feed for free motion, are standard.

checks.title: Confirm the feet in the box
checks.body: Juki lists a zipper foot, an even feed foot and a 1/4 in quilting foot as standard and the 1/5 in foot as optional. Several dealers and reviewers say both quilting feet ship, so ask for the packing list before paying for a bonus kit.

faqs.q: How fast is the Juki TL-2010Q?
faqs.a: Juki publishes a top speed of 1,500 stitches per minute, with a slider that sets any speed from 200 spm. That is the spec, not a promise of finished quality at that speed; heavy layers want a slower setting.

faqs.q: What stitches does the TL-2010Q have?
faqs.a: Straight stitch only, single needle lockstitch, up to 6 mm long. There is no zigzag or buttonhole; plan a second machine for those.

faqs.q: How much throat space does the TL-2010Q have?
faqs.a: Dealers quote 8.5 in by 6 in from the needle to the body. Juki publishes no throat figure, and its machine depth is 8.6 in, so treat 8.5 in as a dealer number. About 6 in is a typical beginner machine; 16 in and up is mid-arm territory.

faqs.q: Does the TL-2010Q come with the 1/5 in quilting foot?
faqs.a: Juki's manual lists a zipper foot, an even feed foot and a 1/4 in quilting foot as standard, and Juki's accessory list shows the 1/5 in quilting foot as optional. Several dealers and reviewers say both ship, so ask the seller for the packing list.

faqs.q: How often does the TL-2010Q need oiling?
faqs.a: Juki's manual says to apply a few drops of the supplied oil at each marked point once a day if you use the machine every day, then test sew. Owners also describe oiling as a habit to learn.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the TL-2010Q and the TL-2000Qi?
faqs.a: Sources agree that the 2010Q adds the front speed slider and a sub-tension unit, for roughly $300 more at dealers. Whether the 2010Q also ships with extra quilting feet is disputed; see the sibling table on this page and the head-to-head.

Dealers publish 5 years limited on parts except electrical and 2 years on motors, light, wiring, switches, circuit boards and speed control. Juki's product page and manual do not state terms, and service runs through authorized dealers, so confirm the seller's status before you buy.
Anyone for whom it would be the only machine. No zigzag, no buttonholes, no stretch stitch.
